agenda_text:
PLANNING COMMISSION AGENDA
  CITY OF AVALON
  Wednesday, January 19, 2022 at 5:00 p.m.
  410 Avalon Canyon Road, Avalon

 In compliance with the Americans with Disability Act, if you need special assistance to participate in
 this meeting, please contact Denise Radde, City Clerk (310) 510-0220. Notification 48 hours prior to the
 meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.
 (28 CFR 35. 102-35.104 ADA Title II). All public records relating to an agenda item on this agenda are
 available for the public inspection at the time the records are distributed to all, or a majority of all,
 members of the Planning Commission. Such records shall be available at City Hall located at 410 Avalon
 Canyon Road.

Due to health recommendations from the Center for Disease Control and State of California
Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), and the declared state of emergency
wherein social distancing measures have been imposed or recommended, the CITY OF
AVALON'S CITY COUNCIL and PLANNING COMMISSION MEETINGS SHALL
GENERALLY BE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC REMOTELY. The general public may attend
the meeting in the Council Chambers however must adhere to social distancing requirements and
wear a mask or face covering at all times. The public is encouraged to watch and participate from
the safety of their homes while practicing social distancing.

Council Chambers are open to a maximum 30 members of the general public. Once the Council
Chambers reach maximum occupancy, the general public may participate in Oral Communication
and address the Planning Commission on an agenda item in-person by waiting in the City Hall
Court Yard and entering the Chambers one at a time at the appropriate time. No one will be
admitted into the Council Chambers who is ill or exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19. All
individuals entering the Council Chambers must wear a mask or face covering at all times.
Additionally, the general public may participate in Oral Communication and address the Planning
Commission on an agenda item by providing comments via e-Comment.

  The meeting can be viewed:
  On local cable: Catalina Broadband Solutions channel 3
  Streaming Online: www.cityofavalon.com/meetings
  *Streaming on Facebook Live: www.facebook.com/CityOfAvalonOfficial
  To submit comments using eComment, please follow this link:
  https://avalon.granicusideas.com
  Click the Meetings tab and then Post to comment on the 01/19/2022 meeting

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE/ROLL CALL

CONSENT CALENDAR

  1. MINUTES
   Although the live recording is the official record of public meetings, actions are prepared
  for the Planning Commission’s approval.

  Recommended Action
  Approve the actions from the December 22, 2021 regular Planning Commission Meeting.

2. Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual Planning Commission
  Meeitings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the December 22, 2021 Planning Commission meeting, the Planning Commission of
  the City of Avalon made findings pursuant to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet
  remotely. To continue this practice, it is required, that the Planning Commission determine
  that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists and has
  been considered by the Planning Commission in deciding to continue to have
  teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
  measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result
  of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health
  or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every thirty (30) days, the
  Planning Commission will have to make these findings at its upcoming February 16, 2022
  meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.

  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists
  and has been considered by the Planning Commission in deciding to continue to have
  teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
  measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result
  of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health
  or safety of attendees.

GENERAL BUSINESS:

1. A Public Hearing for an application for a Transient Rental License and a Coastal
  Development Permit to allow the renting or leasing of a room or rooms with or without
  table boards for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days duration (Transient
  Rental – Section 9-6.602(a) of the Avalon Municipal Code) for unit 64 Gaviota, located
  in building eighteen (18) within the Hamilton Cove Condominiums, and approving a
  resolution. The project is in the Coastal Zone and is subject to a Coastal Development
  Permit, which requires a public hearing and Planning Commission approval. The Planning
  Commission will determine whether the project is within the 300-foot appealable seaward
  area boundary. The project is Categorically Exempt under Section 15305 of the State
  CEQA Guidelines – Minor Alterations in Land Use Limitations.

  Owner/Applicant: Eileen A Lucio and Bradley J Hill
  Filing Date:  12/12/2021
  Location of Project: Unit 64 Gaviota, located in building eighteen (18) of the Hamilton
  Cove Condominiums.
   APN:  7480-047-061
  PC #:  2773
  Zone:  Low-Density Residential

2. A Public Hearing for an application for a Transient Rental License and a Coastal
  Development Permit to allow the renting or leasing of a room or rooms with or without
  table boards for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days duration (Transient
  Rental – Section 9-6.602(a) of the Avalon Municipal Code) for unit 31 Camino de Flores
  located in building two (2) within the Hamilton Cove Condominiums, and approving a
  resolution. The project is in the Coastal Zone and is subject to a Coastal Development
  Permit, which requires a public hearing and Planning Commission approval. The Planning
  Commission will determine whether the project is within the 300-foot appealable seaward
  area boundary. The project is Categorically Exempt under Section 15305 of the State
  CEQA Guidelines – Minor Alterations in Land Use Limitations.

  Owner/Applicant: Phillip Myers and Jeremy Simpson
  Filing Date:  12/22/2021
  Location of Project: Unit 31, Camino de Flores located in building two (2) of the
  Hamilton Cove Condominiums
  APN:  7480-049-094
  PC #:  2774
  Zone:  Low-Density Residential
3. A Public Hearing to consider General Plan Amendment GPA 21-01, approving the 2021-
  2029 planning cycle Housing Element Update and adopting a resolution recommending
  adoption of those changes to the City Council. In compliance with CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15164 an Addendum to the General Plan FEIR has been prepared which
  concludes that the proposed updates to the General Plan Housing Element do not result in
  any new or greater environmental impacts than were previously analyzed, disclosed, and
  mitigated, which will also be considered by the Planning Commission.

  Owner/Applicant: City of Avalon; De Novo Planning Group
  Location of Project: All lands incorporated in the City
  PC #:  2775

4. A Public Hearing to consider Zoning Ordinance Amendment ZOA 22-01 and changes to
  City’s Subdivision titlewithin the Avalon Municipal Code to incorporate “urban lot splits”
  and two-unit projects, as defined in SB9 and required by State law, and to approve a
  resolution recommending adoption of those changes to the City Council. The adoption of
  this proposed ordinance is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (“CEQA”) pursuant to Section 15358 of the State CEQA Guidelines—the project will not
  result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment
  and Section 15061(b)(3), there exists no possibility that the activity will have a significant
  adverse effect on the environment. Additionally, the action is statutorily exempt from
  CEQA pursuant to Government Code sections 65852.21(j) and 66411.7(n).

  Owner/Applicant:  City of Avalon; BB&K
   Location of Project: All residentially zoned property within the City
  PC #:  2776

ITEMS OF DISCUSSION:

PLANNING DIRECTOR / CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

COMMISSIONER BUSINESS

BUSINESS FROM THE AUDIENCE

ADJOURN

Anyone may appeal any decision made by the Commission to the City Council. To appeal, you
must file a written appeal, and include an appeal fee of $1027.00 with the City Clerk within
fifteen (15) calendar days of such action. Any person challenging actions of the Planning
Commission may be limited to issues he or someone else raises in writing prior to or orally at the
hearing. Any person may appeal the Planning Commission’s determination that a proposed
project is seaward of the appealable seaward area boundary to the Coastal Commission, and
following exhaustion of local appeals, any aggrieved person may appeal actions on local Coastal
Development Permits seaward of the appealable area boundary to the Coastal Commission.

By: Rocio De La Cruz  Posted: City Hall  Friday, January 14, 2022
